title: Orientation Session Artifact v0.1
description: A multi-turn orientation session: the answer history, the constraints it projects to, and the propagation and question set that history produces. A standalone artifact: it says its own `kind`. The two embedded artifacts are referenced rather than re-declared, because they ARE those artifacts — `session_to_dict` calls the two producers — and a second declaration of the same shape is the pair of tables that were once equal. Answers are kept as history rather than folded into the constraints: a later answer on the same pair overrides an earlier one, and only the history can say which of two contradicting answers the session is standing on.

answers.description: Every answer ever ingested, in the order it arrived. Replayed in full on each ingest, so the session is a function of this list and its inputs alone.

constraints.description: What the answer history projects to: the latest directional answer per pair, in the order those latest answers appeared. Derived, and recorded so the derivation can be checked.

asserted_adjacencies.description: Turn-0 knowledge, plus whatever per-turn `adjacency` answers have overridden pair by pair.

propagation.description: The Phase 1 artifact this session's constraints produce, embedded verbatim so `verify_orientation_propagation` can audit it in place.

question_set.description: The Phase 2 artifact compiled from that propagation, embedded verbatim for the same reason. Its `questions` are ALL of them; `deferred` below is what removes the ones nobody will answer.

deferred.description: Pairs an answer explicitly declined to decide. Their orientation questions are not worth asking again; their conflicts still are, because a conflict is about the data and not about willingness.

source_trail.description: One entry per answer that was APPLIED, recording what else that answer entailed through the closure. This is the audit of attribution: an answer is responsible not only for its own edge but for everything Meek's rules forced from it.

rejected.description: One entry per directional answer that was NOT applied, and why. The mirror of `source_trail`: between them every directional answer in the history is accounted for exactly once.

status.description: `open`: something is still worth asking. `resolved`: nothing undetermined and nothing to adjudicate. `blocked`: edges remain but every one is deferred — the distinction matters because `blocked` needs a human to change their mind, not another turn.

note.description: What this turn says about itself, one statement per sentence: the counts, then what the status means for what to do next. The second is why `status` above is excused from a gloss — `blocked` and `open` both leave edges undetermined and only one of them is fixed by asking again, which is a difference in what to do rather than a word. A `string` until #469, which is why the sentence was in one language and ended `status=blocked` with the token showing.

edge.description: The pair this answer is about, sorted.

direction.description: The asserted direction, tail-then-head, or null. Always written — an answer that declines to decide says so as null rather than by omission, so that "there is no direction here" has one spelling (#371).

adjacency.description: A claim about whether the pair is connected at all, or null. An answer states a direction OR an adjacency, never both, and null in both fields is the explicit "I do not know" that defers the edge.

source.description: Who said it. Free text, and load-bearing: `orientation_ledger_export` propagates the taint of `llm_proposal` through the closure from exactly this field.

note.description: Whatever the answerer wrote beside their answer. A string, and it stays one where the artifact's own `note` became statements in #469: this is not a sentence the kernel owes a reader, it is a sentence a reader wrote. Its language is whichever one they were writing in, and nothing here may choose it for them.
The answerer's own note, carried through from the answer it came from. A reader's words, not the kernel's — see `answer.note`.

entails.description: The OTHER oriented edges this answer is a root of — its blast radius through the closure, excluding itself.

reason.description: The propagation's reason for refusing this direction, or `not_applied` when the answer simply lost to a later one on the same pair. Echoed as a string rather than re-enumerated here: the vocabulary belongs to the propagation artifact, and `not_applied` is this artifact's own addition to it.
